documents.title: Scan results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI had my first follow up CT for the kidney on the 10th. Urology called, said everything looks clean, no sign of it coming back. Next one in a year or so.

documents.title: RE: Scan results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's great news, thanks for letting me know. I'll ask them to send the report.

documents.title: Urology surveillance letter
documents.author: urology
documents.body: Outside urology. Mr. O'Connell had 6-month surveillance imaging after left partial nephrectomy for pT1b clear cell RCC on 4/10/2024: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast and CT chest show postsurgical change at the left lower pole without recurrence, and no metastatic disease. Next imaging in about 18 months, then yearly. Creatinine stable.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine BP follow-up. April surveillance CT clear per urology letter. Feels well, full duty. Scrotal ache comes and goes, mild. No stones, no gout.
BP per flowsheet at goal. Heart and lungs clear. No edema.
Plan: continue lisinopril 10 and HCTZ 12.5. BMP. Physical in the fall.

reports.text: Right shoulder, three views. No fracture. Glenohumeral and acromioclavicular joints congruent. No dislocation. Soft tissues unremarkable.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital ED, 8/14/2024. Short note.

48M with chronic right rotator cuff pathology, recurrent stones, history of clear cell RCC. Fell off a ladder two days ago and caught himself on his outstretched right arm, felt a sharp pain in the shoulder right away. Since then cannot lift things above shoulder height.
Meds: lisinopril, HCTZ. Allergies: allopurinol, sulfa.

Right shoulder tender anteriorly. Abduction and external rotation clearly weaker than the left. Passive range preserved. Distal neurovascular exam intact.
XR right shoulder: no fracture or dislocation.

Impression: right shoulder injury, likely rotator cuff re-injury.
Sling for comfort, acetaminophen. Follow up with orthopedics this week or next for MRI.

orders.reason: right shoulder re-injury after ladder fall

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED f/u. Fell from a ladder 8/12 onto the outstretched R arm, ED 8/14, x-ray negative. Still can't get the arm above his shoulder. Wearing the sling some of the day. Acetaminophen helps a little.

Exam: R shoulder tender anteriorly, weak abduction and external rotation, passive motion preserved. Neurovascularly intact.

A/P: right shoulder injury on top of the known supraspinatus tear. Re-referred to the same orthopedics clinic; they will image. Work note: no overhead work or lifting over 10 lb with the right arm until seen. Acetaminophen, no NSAIDs.

documents.title: Work note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: To whom it may concern: Matthew O'Connell is under my care for a right shoulder injury. Please restrict him from overhead work and from lifting more than 10 pounds with the right arm until cleared by orthopedics.

documents.title: Orthopedic follow-up
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedics, shoulder clinic. Visit 9/4/2024.
Known to us from 2021 for a right supraspinatus tear treated with therapy. Now after a ladder fall 8/12 onto the outstretched arm, with pain and overhead weakness.
Exam: anterior shoulder tenderness, weak abduction and external rotation, passive range preserved.
MRI right shoulder 8/30/2024: increased signal within the supraspinatus tendon consistent with a tear.
Plan: physical therapy, light duty with no overhead lifting for 6 weeks, acetaminophen. Recheck if not progressing; surgical repair would be discussed then. Allergies: allopurinol, sulfa.

documents.title: Shoulder
documents.author: patient
documents.body: PT going ok, arm getting stronger. Boss has me on the ground crew for now. Can I get the flu shot when I come in for my physical or should I do it sooner?

documents.title: RE: Shoulder
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sooner is better. We have flu and COVID shots on the nurse schedule most mornings. I booked you 10/16 at 7:30.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (trivalent this season) L deltoid, 2024-25 COVID R deltoid, avoided the healing R shoulder for the flu shot. No reactions.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 48M.

This year: right shoulder re-injured in an August ladder fall, MRI again showed the supraspinatus tear, PT through October, back to regular duty early November with some soreness. Kidney surveillance CT in April clear. No stones, no gout flares.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg, HCTZ 12.5 mg, acetaminophen prn. Allergies: sulfa; allopurinol.
SH: construction, quit smoking 2018, 1-2 beers a week.

Exam: well. HEENT normal. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed port scars. R shoulder: abduction full with a painful arc, strength 4+/5. Skin clear. No edema.
PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P:
1. HTN at goal.
2. RCC s/p partial nephrectomy, next CT per urology in fall 2025.
3. R rotator cuff tear, improved after PT.
4. Labs CMP, CBC, lipids. Flu and COVID done. Colonoscopy due 2032. Shingles vaccine at 50.
RTC spring.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill lisinopril 10 mg and HCTZ 12.5 mg. Labs 11/2024 normal. 90 days x1 sent. Pt due for spring BP visit, front desk to call.

conditions.note: 7 mm left ureterovesical junction stone, mild hydronephrosis

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth daily until the stone passes
Dissolve 1 tablet on the tongue every 8 hours as needed for nausea

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 4/7/2025, abbreviated.

48M, recurrent stones, prior left ureteral stone, s/p left partial nephrectomy for RCC. Six hours of severe left flank pain into the groin, nausea and vomiting. No fever or chills. Allergies: allopurinol, sulfa. Meds: lisinopril, HCTZ.

Afebrile, BP 150/90, HR 98. Left CVA tenderness.
UA: hematuria. Creatinine 1.2 (baseline 1.0). WBC 12.0.
CT abdomen/pelvis without contrast: 7 mm stone at the left UVJ with mild hydronephrosis. No signs of infection.

Dx: left UVJ stone.
IV fluids, analgesia and antiemetic in the ED. Home on tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily and ondansetron ODT, acetaminophen. Strain urine. Urology follow-up within 1-2 weeks; return for fever or uncontrolled pain.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED 4/7 for a 7 mm left UVJ stone with mild hydronephrosis, Cr 1.2 there. On tamsulosin since. Hasn't seen it come out yet. Pain now a dull ache, needs acetaminophen at night only. No fever, no vomiting since the first day.

Exam: afebrile, BP per vitals. Mild left CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft.

A/P: left UVJ stone, not yet passed, symptoms improving. Continue tamsulosin. Recheck creatinine today. Urology appointment is 4/23; if not passed by then they will discuss ureteroscopy. Fever, rigors or worsening pain: go back to the ED.
Addendum 16:50: creatinine back to 1.0.

documents.title: Stone
documents.author: patient
documents.body: It passed last night!! Pain is gone. Can I stop the tamsulosin? Should I still go to urology next week?

documents.title: RE: Stone
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great. Yes, you can stop the tamsulosin. Bring the stone to urology; keep that appointment so they can confirm and send it for analysis if they want.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from his truck at lunch, identity verified. BP check deferred to home cuff: he bought one after the ED, readings mostly 128-136 over 78-84 in the mornings. No symptoms. Stone passed in April; urology saw him, no further plans other than hydration. Meds lisinopril 10, HCTZ 12.5.
A/P: HTN controlled on home readings. Continue. In-person physical in the fall with labs.

documents.title: Kidney scan
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Had my 2 year scan Wednesday 10/8, CT of the belly and chest. Urology says still no cancer. Next one in a year. Can you get me in for flu?

documents.title: RE: Kidney scan
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wonderful news. Booked flu shot 10/22 at 7:30.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine given L deltoid. Declined COVID this year, would rather wait. Tolerated.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 49M.

Interval: April left UVJ stone, passed on tamsulosin. October surveillance CT clear per patient and urology. Shoulder holding up, sore after heavy days. No gout flares.

Meds unchanged: lisinopril 10, HCTZ 12.5, acetaminophen prn. Allergies sulfa, allopurinol.
SH: former smoker (quit 2018, 15 pk-yr), light alcohol, construction.

Exam: well. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. R shoulder mild painful arc. No edema. Skin clear.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
1. HTN controlled.
2. RCC surveillance per urology, next fall 2026.
3. Nephrolithiasis, recurrent: fluids.
4. Labs today. Shingrix at 50 next year. Colonoscopy 2032.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Matthew, labs all normal including kidney function and cholesterol. Have a good winter.

conditions.note: left ribs 4 to 7, each fractured in more than two places

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Fractures of the left 4th through 7th ribs, each rib fractured in more than two locations, forming a flail segment. No pneumothorax seen on this supine film. Cardiomediastinal silhouette normal.
reports.conclusion: Multiple segmental left rib fractures, ribs 4 to 7, consistent with flail chest.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 2/12/2026. Copy received with the discharge summary.

49M construction worker, HTN, gout, recurrent kidney stones, chronic R rotator cuff problem (ladder fall 2024). Fell from a second-story scaffold onto his left side. Severe left chest pain, worse breathing in and coughing. No LOC, no headache, no vomiting.

RR 28, tachypneic, distressed. Decreased breath sounds left lower field. Exquisitely tender left chest wall with paradoxical inward motion on inspiration.
ABG: pH 7.45, PaCO2 32, PaO2 60, HCO3 24, sat 90%.
CXR: left ribs 4-7 fractured, each in more than two places.

Impression: flail chest, left. Hypoxemia.
Oxygen, analgesia, trauma surgery consulted. Admitted to ICU.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for severe pain

results.test: Carbon dioxide partial pressure in Arterial blood
Oxygen partial pressure in Arterial blood

reports.text: Portable AP chest in the ICU. Multiple left rib fractures as before. No pneumothorax. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Multiple left rib fractures. No pneumothorax.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 2/12/2026, discharged 2/20/2026.
Diagnoses: left flail chest (ribs 4-7, segmental); acute hypoxemic respiratory failure.

Course: from the ED to the ICU in moderate respiratory distress, RR 28, SpO2 92% on room air, T 37.2, BP 145/90, HR 110, with a deformed left chest wall moving paradoxically and decreased left breath sounds. ABG on arrival pH 7.35, PaCO2 45, PaO2 60, HCO3 24. Repeat CXR: left rib fractures, no pneumothorax. Thoracic epidural placed for analgesia, high-flow nasal cannula, aggressive incentive spirometry and pulmonary toilet. Did not require intubation. Not a candidate for operative rib fixation per trauma surgery. Weaned to room air and moved to the ward 2/16, epidural out 2/18, pain controlled on oral medicine.

Discharge meds: home lisinopril 10 mg and HCTZ 12.5 mg; acetaminophen as needed; oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed, 5-day supply. Avoid NSAIDs.
Allergies: allopurinol, sulfa.
Follow-up: trauma clinic in 3 weeks with chest x-ray; PCP within 1 week. No work until cleared by trauma clinic.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transitional care call. Home since Friday 2/20 after a scaffold fall with left rib fractures, ICU stay. Breathing OK at rest, short of breath climbing his stairs but better each day. Using the spirometer. Taking oxycodone 2-3 times a day plus acetaminophen. No fever, no cough with sputum. Bowels moving. Discharge papers received today. Booked with PCP 2/25. A friend will drive him.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up. Fell from a second-story scaffold 2/12. Left flail chest, ribs 4-7 broken in several places each, hypoxemic respiratory failure; ICU with epidural and high-flow oxygen, no intubation, no surgery. Home 2/20.

Now: pain 5/10, worse with coughing and turning in bed. Oxycodone twice a day, acetaminophen. Breathing better, walks around the house fine, winded on stairs. Spirometer reaching about where the hospital wanted. No fever or sputum.

Meds reconciled: lisinopril 10, HCTZ 12.5, acetaminophen prn, oxycodone 5 mg prn (short supply). Allergies sulfa, allopurinol.

Exam: comfortable at rest, SpO2 on room air per vitals. Left chest wall tender with bruising fading, chest wall moves symmetrically now. Lungs clear, no crackles. Heart regular. No calf tenderness.

A/P:
1. Left flail chest, healing. Keep up incentive spirometer, splint with a pillow to cough. Taper oxycodone over the next week; no refill planned. Acetaminophen scheduled while sore. No NSAIDs (kidney history).
2. Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, resolved, on room air.
3. HTN: BP fine, no changes.
4. Off work until trauma clinic clears him; work note given.
Trauma clinic 3/11.

documents.title: Work note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: To whom it may concern: Matthew O'Connell is recovering from injuries sustained 2/12/2026 and is unable to work. His return date will be set by his trauma surgery team.

documents.title: Trauma clinic note
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body: Trauma surgery clinic, seen 3/11/2026. Four weeks after left flail chest. Pain improving, off oxycodone. Lungs clear. CXR today: healing left rib fractures 4-7, no effusion, no pneumothorax. Plan: progressive activity, no lifting over 20 lb for 4 more weeks, then graded return to work. Follow up as needed.

documents.title: Work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Done with the oxycodone, just Tylenol now. Trauma clinic said light duty in May. My employer wants a note from you too saying I can't work until then. Can you send one?

documents.title: RE: Work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Done, the note is attached in your portal letters. Keep walking every day. Let us know if the breathing gets worse instead of better.

documents.title: Back to work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Back on light duty as of Monday. Ribs only sore at the end of the day. Staying off ladders for now, believe me. Do I need to see you before my physical?

documents.title: RE: Back to work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good to hear. No, unless something changes. Let's do your physical in early summer; you turn 50 this month so we'll start the shingles shots.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill lisinopril 10 mg, HCTZ 12.5 mg. Last labs 11/2025 normal. Physical booked 7/10. Sent 90 days.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 50M.

Interval: February scaffold fall with left flail chest and hypoxemic respiratory failure, ICU, no intubation. Off opioids since March. Back on light duty since early May, now doing most of his old job except high work. Ribs ache after long days, breathing normal, no cough. Shoulder about the same. No stones since April 2025, no gout flares. Kidney surveillance CT due this fall with urology.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, HCTZ 12.5 mg daily, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: sulfa; allopurinol (AIN).
SH: quit smoking 2018, 15 pack-years. 1-2 drinks weekly. Construction.

ROS otherwise negative.
Exam: well. HEENT normal. Neck supple. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally, good air movement. Chest wall: mild tenderness left lateral ribs, no deformity. Abdomen soft, healed port scars. R shoulder mild painful arc, strength good. No edema. Skin clear.
PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P:
1. HTN, controlled. Continue.
2. Left flail chest, healed clinically; respiratory failure resolved.
3. Clear cell RCC s/p partial nephrectomy, surveillance through urology.
4. Recurrent nephrolithiasis, gout: quiet.
5. R rotator cuff tear, chronic, functional.
6. Prevention: Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months. Colonoscopy due 2032. CMP, CBC, lipids.
RTC 1 year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Matthew, your labs from Friday are normal: kidney function steady, blood count and cholesterol fine. Nothing to change.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. Arm was sore from the shingles shot for 2 days, figured that's normal.

documents.title: Pharmacy fill history
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy confirmed auto-refill of lisinopril 10 mg and HCTZ 12.5 mg picked up 8/9. No action needed.

documents.title: Shingles shot
documents.author: patient
documents.body: When should I get the second shingles shot? Fall works better for me, work is crazy right now.

documents.title: RE: Shingles shot
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Anytime from September through early January is fine. Call or message when you know your schedule and we'll put you on the nurse schedule, and we can do your flu shot the same morning.
